sentences.text: Revenue, net interest income plus noninterest income, grew from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025 [D5][D206], a 7.3% CAGR.
Net interest income compounded at 8.4% and noninterest income at 6.2% over the window [F111][F112].
The path was a step change, not a smooth compound: revenue rose 22.9% in FY2023 [D179] and 12.3% in FY2024 [D202], after a 1.4% gain in FY2021 [D129].
The FY2023 step came from higher rates lifting net interest income, with Payments revenue up 22% on deposit margin expansion [P37] and net interest income up 33.8% [D174].
FY2025 growth slowed to 2.8% [D226] as net interest income rose 3.1% [D221] and noninterest income 2.4% [D222].
North America supplied 76.6% of FY2025 revenue [D249] but only 0.2pp of that year's growth [D251], while EMEA added 1.2pp [D276] and Asia-Pacific 1.2pp [D301].

FY2025 net interest income growth came from higher Markets net interest income, higher Card Services revolving balances and higher wholesale deposit balances, largely offset by deposit margin compression [P28].
Noninterest income rose 2% on higher Markets revenue, asset management fees and investment banking fees, offset by the absence of the $7.9 billion Visa gain booked in FY2024 [P27].
Noninterest expense grew 4.2% against 2.8% revenue growth in FY2025 [D225][D226], so the incremental margin was negative.
Diluted EPS rose 1.4% in FY2025 [D216] while net income fell 2.6% [D214], because the diluted share count shrank 3.4% [D224].
The efficiency ratio was 52.4% in FY2025 [D207], below its 57.2% window median [D333] and near the 51.7% window low set in FY2024 [D331].
That sits well below the banks peer median of 61.7% [D337], the best efficiency ratio in the seven-bank group [D336].
Noninterest expense rose 4% on higher compensation, brokerage and distribution fees, auto lease depreciation and technology and marketing spend [P26].
The credit-loss provision was 7.8% of revenue in FY2025 [D208], up from 6.0% in FY2024 [D185] and above the 6.0% peer median [D341].

The higher provision reflected net increases in loan and commitment portfolios, credit-quality changes on client-specific exposures, and estimated losses from borrower fraud in secured lending facilities [P15].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank; it was negative $148 billion in FY2025 [F60] against $57.0 billion of net income [F30].

The FY2025 outflow came from higher trading assets, higher securities borrowed, net loan originations held-for-sale and higher other assets, partly offset by net income and higher trading liabilities [P21].
Capital return is the better test: buybacks plus dividends of $48.2 billion [D205] were 0.85x FY2025 net income [F30].
Return on average equity was 16.1% in FY2025 [D213], the 100th percentile of the seven-bank peer group against an 11.8% median [D338][D339].
Loans were 57.3% of deposits in FY2025 [D211], up from 43.1% in FY2021 [D115] as deposit growth outran lending in the pandemic years.
Loans rose $121 billion, driven by higher CIB Markets loans and securities-based lending in AWM on higher client demand [P4].
FY2025 buybacks of $31.6 billion [X102] and dividends of $16.6 billion [X112] totaled $48.2 billion [D205], and the diluted share count fell 3.4% [D224].
Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy's pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, and differs by up to 0.10% [R1][F30][X20].
The gap is immaterial to the trend, but FY2025 net income is $57.0 billion in the table [F30] against $57.0 billion as filed [X20].
The provision rose to 7.8% of revenue [D208] while criticized wholesale exposure grew to $48.5 billion, about 3.4% of wholesale credit exposure [P2].
Criticized exposure rose on downgrades and new commitments in SPEs, Consumer & Retail, Banks & Finance Companies, Healthcare and Chemicals & Plastics [P2].
Watch the efficiency ratio: a move back above the 57.2% window median [D333] would reverse the FY2024-FY2025 improvement, reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Watch the credit-loss provision: a further rise above 7.8% of revenue [D208] would extend the FY2024-FY2025 climb, disclosed in the FY2026 10-K.
Watch net interest income: a decline from $95.4 billion [F10] would break the FY2022-FY2025 run, reported in the FY2026 10-K.
